newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sold off on back of NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sold off on back of NYMEX.

text.p: IPE July Brent dipped back into negative territory after a brief move upwards as selling on NYMEX crude was followed in London, brokers said.
The prompt Brent contract moved back down to $19.90 a barrel, down 10 cents from the open by 1604 gmt.
"There's no volume worth talking about on the NYMEX or Brent (IPE)," one broker said.

He added that the draw on U.S. crude oil stocks for last week seen both in the American Petroleum Institute's (API's) and U.S Department of Energy (DOE) was partly a correction to last weeks statistics.
In addition a large part of the draw was in West Coast PADD 5 which was "ignored by people".
June gas oil on the IPE lost ground as well, moving last off $1.75 at $176.00 a tonne.
DOE crude stocks for the week ending May 16 were down 5.4 million barrels while the overnight API's showed a draw of 5.9 million barrels.
